title: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
capsule: The Eastern Hungarian Kingdom emerged after the Ottoman victory at Mohács (August 1526) when John Zápolya was elected king by Diet opponents to Habsburg succession and swore fealty to Sultan Suleiman I in 1529, controlling Transylvania and the eastern counties as an Ottoman client. After John's death in 1540 his infant son John II Sigismund reigned under the regency of Queen Isabella and Bishop Martinuzzi; the 1538 Treaty of Nagyvárad had partitioned Hungary but Ottoman occupation of Buda in 1541 entrenched the division. John II issued the Edict of Torda in 1568, the first European statute recognizing freedom of conscience for four Christian confessions. Under the Treaty of Speyer (1570) John II renounced the royal title and was recognized as Prince of Transylvania, transforming the realm into the Principality of Transylvania.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The general extent of the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom is well established from Ottoman, Habsburg, and Transylvanian administrative sources; the exact boundaries of disputed border counties fluctuated with military campaigns and are mapped with moderate precision.
